intro: A probability of 0.8 should correspond to a similar observed positive fraction across many comparable forecasts. Inspect that agreement in bins.
task: Group binary forecasts into equal-width probability bins and return counts, mean probabilities, positive fractions, and weighted absolute calibration error.
requirements: labels and probabilities are nonempty same-length finite vectors. Labels are zero or one and probabilities lie in [0,1]. num_bins is a positive integer excluding booleans.
Bin index is min(floor(probability * num_bins), num_bins - 1). Boundaries enter the bin on their right, except probability one stays in the final bin.
Return counts, mean_probability, and positive_fraction as NumPy vectors plus ece as a scalar. Empty bins have zero means and fractions and contribute zero error.
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Assign each probability to a bin, explicitly clipping probability one to the final index.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Accumulate counts and two sums, divide only occupied bins, then weight absolute gaps by counts/n.

explanation: A reliability table groups forecasts with similar predicted probabilities and compares their mean forecast with the observed fraction of positive outcomes.
The requested error weights each bin’s absolute gap by its share of observations. Empty bins carry no evidence and no weight; their zero values are placeholders.
Change the number of bins on a small sample. Explain why the estimate changes, why a low binned error is not proof of calibration, and why this diagnostic should accompany discrimination metrics.
